# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 76

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Disagreement 1 — "brought from the deep" — source of the deep stones

- **EMET:** "brought from the deep"
- **LOGOS:** "brought from the deep"
- **PNEUMA:** "brought up from the deep"
- **Greek:** *ek tou bythou* — "from the deep/depth"
- **Ruling:** All agents agree on the substance. SOPHIA uses "brought from the deep" (EMET/LOGOS). "From the deep" is sufficient; "up from" (PNEUMA) is implied.

---

## Disagreement 2 — "joined well with" vs. "fit with"

- **EMET:** "fit with the stones that were put in from the plain"
- **LOGOS:** "joined well with the stones already set in from the plain"
- **PNEUMA:** "fit perfectly with the ones from the plain"
- **Greek:** *synērmozonto meta tōn lithōn* — "were fitted/joined together with the stones"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "joined well with the stones already set in from the plain" (LOGOS). *Synarmozō* means "to fit together/join" — "joined well" captures both the action and quality; "fit perfectly" (PNEUMA) is slightly over-emphatic.

---

## Disagreement 3 — "could not be used in the building" vs. "unusable"

- **EMET:** "could not be used in the building"
- **LOGOS:** "could not be used in the structure"
- **PNEUMA:** "unusable"
- **Greek:** *ou sunērmozonto eis tēn oikodomēn* — "were not fitting for the construction"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "could not be used in the structure" (LOGOS). "Structure" (*oikodomē*) is more precise than the general "building"; PNEUMA's one-word summary "unusable" loses the architectural specificity.

---

## Disagreement 4 — "clothe him" vs. "clothe him with their garment"

- **EMET:** "clothe him"
- **LOGOS:** "clothe him with their garment"
- **PNEUMA:** "clothed by them"
- **Greek:** *endysōsin auton* — "clothe him"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "clothe him" (EMET). The garment is implied by the clothing verb; LOGOS's addition "with their garment" is explanatory but redundant in context.

---

## Disagreement 5 — "it profits you nothing" vs. "it does you no good"

- **EMET:** "it profits you nothing"
- **LOGOS:** "it profits you nothing"
- **PNEUMA:** "it does you no good"
- **Greek:** *ouden soi ōphelei* — "it benefits/profits you nothing"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "it profits you nothing" (EMET/LOGOS). "Profits" is the established translation of *ōpheleō* in this doctrinal context (cf. 1 Cor 13:3).

---

## Disagreement 6 — "carry his name in vain" vs. "bearing the name for nothing"

- **EMET:** "you will bear his name in vain"
- **LOGOS:** "you will carry his name in vain"
- **PNEUMA:** "you're carrying the name for nothing"
- **Greek:** *matēn phereis to onoma autou* — "in vain you carry his name"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "you will carry his name in vain" (LOGOS). "In vain" (*matēn*) is the precise term; "for nothing" (PNEUMA) is colloquial but slightly weakens the theological gravity.

---

## Disagreement 7 — "the names themselves are the garment"

- **EMET:** "the names themselves are the garment"
- **LOGOS:** "the names themselves are the garment"
- **PNEUMA:** "the names themselves are the garment"
- **Greek:** *ta onomata autōn himation estin* — "their names are the garment"
- **Ruling:** All agents agree. No ruling needed. SOPHIA preserves "the names themselves are the garment" as the literal and theologically precise rendering.

---

## Disagreement 8 — "abandoned the true road" vs. "gave up the true road"

- **EMET:** "abandoned their true road"
- **LOGOS:** "abandoned the true road"
- **PNEUMA:** "gave up the true road"
- **Greek:** *apeleipon tēn hodon tēn alēthinēn* — "abandoned the true road"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "abandoned the true road" (LOGOS). "Abandoned" (*apoleipō*) is the correct translation; PNEUMA's "gave up" is slightly casual.

---

## Disagreement 9 — "were afflicted" vs. "suffered" vs. "ended up suffering"

- **EMET:** "were tormented"
- **LOGOS:** "were afflicted"
- **PNEUMA:** "ended up suffering out there in the rough terrain"
- **Greek:** *ebasanizonto* — "were tormented/afflicted"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "were afflicted" (LOGOS). *Basanizō* ranges from "torment" to "afflict/distress" — "afflicted" is more measured than "tormented," which implies extreme physical pain; PNEUMA's expansion is interpretive.

---

## Disagreement 10 — "fully apostatized" vs. "completely walked away"

- **EMET:** "completely apostasized from the living God"
- **LOGOS:** "fully apostatized from the living God"
- **PNEUMA:** "completely walked away from the living God"
- **Greek:** *holotelos apestēsan apo tou Theou tou zōntos* — "wholly departed from the living God"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "fully apostatized from the living God" (LOGOS). "Apostatized" is the technical term for this final, complete departure; PNEUMA's "walked away" softens what the Greek presents as total apostasy.

---

## Disagreement 11 — "drew back" vs. "changed their minds" vs. "backed away"

- **EMET:** "they changed their minds and went back"
- **LOGOS:** "they drew back and went off again"
- **PNEUMA:** "they backed away and went right back"
- **Greek:** *apestraphēsan kai palin eporeuthēsan* — "they turned away and went again"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "they drew back and went off again after their evil desires" (LOGOS). "Drew back" captures the turning (*apostrephō*) precisely; "changed their minds" (EMET) implies a cognitive shift rather than a volitional turning away.

---

*Disagreement log generated 2026-03-17. SOPHIA rulings are binding for the consensus text.*
